# Kyoto 5-Day Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A relaxed, temple-and-garden focused Kyoto itinerary for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14** with **one hotel base**, **moderate pace**, and **3 major activities max per day**.
Budget target: **$2,400 USD total, excluding international flights**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Arrival + Gion + Kiyomizu-dera
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Kyoto, check into one central hotel, and have a light lunch near Kyoto Station or Gion.
- Afternoon: Walk the preserved streets of **Gion** and **Higashiyama** at an easy pace.
- Evening: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** for sunset views, then enjoy a traditional dinner nearby.

Action: [Button: Hotel search](https://www.booking.com/city/jp/kyoto.en-gb.html)

### Day 2: Arashiyama Gardens + Bamboo Grove
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Start early at the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Visit **Tenryu-ji Garden** and stroll the river area or Togetsukyo Bridge.
- Evening: Have a relaxed kaiseki-style or tofu-focused dinner in western Kyoto.

Action: [Button: Arashiyama map](https://www.google.com/maps/search/Arashiyama,+Kyoto)

### Day 3: Northern Kyoto Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Explore **Kinkaku-ji**.
- Afternoon: Continue to **Ryoan-ji** for the rock garden, then take a slow break at a nearby café or lunch spot.
- Evening: Keep the night light with an easy neighborhood dinner and rest.

Action: [Button: Temple route](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/Kinkaku-ji,+Kyoto/Ryoan-ji,+Kyoto)

### Day 4: Philosopher’s Path + Zen Gardens
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Walk part of the **Philosopher’s Path** and visit **Ginkaku-ji**.
- Afternoon: Add one more garden/temple stop such as **Nanzen-ji** or a tea break in Okazaki.
- Evening: Enjoy local Kyoto dishes such as yuba, obanzai, or ramen in the city center.

Action: [Button: Kyoto food spots](https://www.google.com/maps/search/Kyoto+local+food)

### Day 5: Nishiki Market + Final Temple Stop + Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Browse **Nishiki Market** for snacks, pickles, sweets, and souvenirs.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Browse **Nishiki Market** for snacks, pickles, sweets, and souvenirs, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Fit in one final nearby temple or garden if timing allows, then return to the hotel for checkout.
- Evening: Depart Kyoto or transfer to your next destination.

## Cost Estimate by Category

| Category | Estimate for 2 Adults | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel, 4 nights | **$900–$1,200** | One mid-range hotel in central Kyoto or near Kyoto Station |
| Local transport | **$80–$140** | Subway, buses, occasional taxi |
| Admissions | **$60–$120** | Temples, gardens, and a few paid sights |
| Food | **$420–$650** | Mix of casual meals, market snacks, and one nicer dinner |
| Snacks, tea, extras | **$60–$120** | Coffee, sweets, small purchases |
| Buffer | **$150–$250** | Weather, taxi, or extra meal flexibility |

### Budget Fit
- **Likely total:** **$1,670–$2,480**
- To stay within **$2,400**, aim for:
  - hotel around **$900–$1,050**
  - food around **$450–$550**
  - transport and admissions kept moderate

## Practical Planning Notes

- **Stay location:** Best single-hotel base is **Kyoto Station**, **Karasuma**, or **Gion/Shijo** for easy transit and dining.
- **Cherry blossom timing:** Your dates are in a high-demand spring window; book hotel and key dinner reservations early.
- **Pace control:** Limit each day to **2–3 major stops** and build in tea breaks or short walks.
- **Transit:** Kyoto buses can be crowded in spring; use **subway + taxi** selectively to save time.
- **Temple hours:** Many sites open early and close by late afternoon, so keep morning temple visits and evening food plans.
- **Food strategy:** Mix one sit-down meal daily with market snacks or casual lunches to stay on budget.
- **Weather readiness:** April can be mild but changeable; bring a light jacket and comfortable walking shoes.
